headline: Highest risk is data leakage: next-ai-draw-io can call external APIs and handle API keys, while awesome-prompts is a prompt repository with no runtime isolation or egress, creating a plausible cross-agent exfiltration path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a prompt/content repository, so its outputs can contain attacker-controlled instructions. next-ai-draw-io uses natural-language commands and MCP/browser tooling, which can be steered if it ingests prompt text or copied content. No shared channel is documented, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF outputs from awesome-prompts are pasted into next-ai-draw-io prompts or MCP inputs, instruction hijacking is plausible.
IF next-ai-draw-io treats repository text as authoritative instructions, prompt injection can succeed.
mitigations: Require manual review before pasting prompt text into next-ai-draw-io.
Prefix imported text as data, not instructions.
Disable MCP for untrusted prompt ingestion sessions.
Use a separate workspace for prompt curation.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress and explicit API-key handling, so it can transmit content to third-party model APIs. awesome-prompts is a content source that may be copied into that workflow. The pair lacks documented isolation, so leakage is plausible in default use, though not proven from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF awesome-prompts content is loaded into next-ai-draw-io and sent to a remote model API, that content may leave the local environment.
IF API keys are configured for next-ai-draw-io, remote transmission can occur through its documented API surfaces.
mitigations: Avoid sending sensitive prompt text to remote APIs.
Use a local-only model backend where possible.
Rotate any API keys used in testing.
Review outbound destinations before processing imported content.
requires-engineering: add per-document egress controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is not runnable and shows no write surfaces, while next-ai-draw-io supports multiple instances but only documents file and API interactions. There is no documented shared writable directory or overlapping mutable resource, so direct capability conflict appears limited.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write to the same directory or diagram file, conflicts become possible.
IF an external orchestrator shares mutable state between them, write contention can occur.
mitigations: Keep separate working directories.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same file.
Use file locking in the orchestrator.
Export before importing between tools.
requires-engineering: add coordination locks for shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts can supply prompt templates or instructions, and next-ai-draw-io uses AI-assisted visualization with natural-language commands. If next-ai-draw-io treats imported prompts as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect diagrams or actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io uses awesome-prompts output as a template without verification, downstream diagram errors can propagate.
IF generated diagrams are used as source-of-truth, incorrect content can cascade into later work products.
mitigations: Verify generated diagrams against source documents.
Require human approval before exporting.
Separate prompt templates from factual source material.
Use a review checklist for AI-generated diagrams.
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability links from outputs to sources.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io explicitly handles API keys and can send files to external APIs, while awesome-prompts is a public content repository with no stated residency or retention controls. If regulated or sensitive documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io, compliance gaps can arise from remote processing and logging. The other agent is not cited separately because it is only a content source here.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed through next-ai-draw-io's remote API surfaces, residency or retention obligations may be violated.
IF API-provider logging retains uploaded content, subject-rights or retention requirements may be impacted.
mitigations: Use only approved regions/providers.
Avoid uploading regulated documents.
Check provider retention settings.
Document data-processing agreements before use.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention enforcement.
